chunks: From him, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī Maryam, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “O Abā Maryam, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has written a document for Ibn Ḥazm regarding the charities, so take it from him and bring it to me so that I may look at it.”

He said: So I went to him and took the document from him, then I brought it to him and presented it before him. In it were chapters on charities and chapters on blood-money, and in it was: “For the eye, fifty; for the jāʾifah wound, one-third; for the munaqqilah, fifteen; and for the mūḍiḥah, five camels.”

key_terms.الصَّدَقَاتِ: charitable dues or alms discussed in the written document
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit used here for legal compensation
key_terms.الْجَائِفَةِ: a penetrating wound reaching the body cavity
key_terms.الْعَيْنِ: the eye, for which a specific compensation is stated
key_terms.الْمُنَقِّلَةِ: an injury that displaces or transfers bone
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Ibn Ḥazm’s document say about diyah for eye injuries and head wounds?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام directing Abū Maryam to retrieve a written document attributed to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله concerning alms and legal compensations. It preserves specific rulings on diyāt for certain bodily injuries, showing the use of documented Prophetic tradition in legal matters.
